calls.headline: Pound slips to 54.50 and EGX30 breaks 50,000 on local selling
calls.body: The central bank's selling rate rose 63 piastres to EGP 54.50 from 53.87 at Thursday's close (Manassa, Youm7), and the EGX30 fell 2.85% to 49,989.79, its fourth straight loss, while the EGX70 EWI lost 5.55%; 205 stocks fell and 4 rose on EGP 6.6bn of turnover (Arab Finance, Al-Borsa). Foreign investors were net buyers of EGP 158.3m (Arab Finance); by type, Egyptian institutions sold a net EGP 181.1m and foreign institutions bought EGP 170.1m (Osoul Misr). Manassa ties the pound's fall to demand for imports and debt repayments; the central bank gave no reason.
calls.view: A leveraged, local sell-off rather than foreign flight: foreign institutions bought, and Al-Borsa puts margin loans near EGP 17bn, so forced selling can run a session or two before it burns out. The pound is the part to watch: a 1.2% move in one step, with a Fed hike about 89% priced for December 9 and the US 10-year at 4.94%, says dollar demand is outrunning supply, though the IMF board vote due before December 15 is near-term support. The desk expects the EGX30 to steady above 48,000 and the dollar to stay under EGP 56 into the vote. Low confidence on the index, medium on the pound.
calls.wrong: The EGX30 closes below 48,000, or the dollar above EGP 56, before December 15.
calls.notice: The margin-loan figure comes from one analyst quoted by Al-Borsa, and the reason for the pound's move is Manassa's reading, not the central bank's; the view does not rely on either.

calls.headline: Bills clear at 26.29% and the state weighs a 19.5% sukuk
calls.line: The central bank took EGP 104bn of 273-day bills against an EGP 80bn target, at about the year's highest yield.
calls.body: At Sunday's auction the central bank sold 273-day bills at 26.29%, accepting EGP 104bn against an EGP 80bn target, and 91-day bills at 24.92%, EGP 140.5bn in all (Amwal Al Ghad, Arab Finance). Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk ordered a study of raising the next tax sukuk's yield half a point to 19.5%, the Tax Authority said; it is a study, with no size or date (Daily News Egypt, Al-Masry Al-Youm).
calls.view: Demand is there, but at a price: the state taking more than it planned at above 26% says it needs the money and will pay for it, which makes a cut on December 17 unlikely with a Fed hike due on December 9. Banks with large bill books keep earning; developers and consumer lenders get no relief this year. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: The central bank cuts its deposit rate on December 17, or the 273-day yield falls below 25% at an auction before then.

calls.headline: Three LNG cargoes turn away from Egypt as Europe pays more
calls.line: Fewer cargoes keep gas tight for fertilizer makers; Abu Qir fell 3.1% and MOPCO 5.3% on Sunday.
calls.body: Three LNG tankers bound for Egyptian terminals changed course in recent days, two toward Europe, where buyers pay more, EnterpriseAM reported from Bloomberg ship-tracking data compiled with Kpler. Abu Qir fell 3.1% to EGP 74.00 and MOPCO 5.3% to EGP 36.21, its lowest since July; CI Capital kept neutral ratings on both while raising its 12-month targets to EGP 85.4 and EGP 42.1 (Economy Plus).
calls.view: Each lost cargo makes it harder to restore the gas cut from fertilizer plants, whose gas already costs 50% more, $12.75 per mmBtu, until December 31; the desk keeps its view that the sector stays under pressure through November. Low confidence: the diversions rest on one report, and urea near $510 a ton still leaves export margins.
calls.wrong: Abu Qir closes above EGP 85 before November 30.
calls.notice: The diversions are reported by one outlet from ship-tracking data, and CI Capital's targets by one outlet; the view rests on the gas price already confirmed in Abu Qir's disclosure.

calls.headline: Misr Life valued at EGP 69.1bn ahead of a December sale
calls.line: EGP 13.82 a share; selling 15% would raise about EGP 10.4bn, the desk's arithmetic.
calls.body: A government committee valued Misr Life Insurance at about EGP 69.1bn, EGP 13.82 a share, an unnamed official told Asharq Business, and the company confirmed it plans to sell 15%, 750 million existing shares, in December (Arab Finance, Zawya). At that value the sale is about EGP 10.4bn, more than one and a half of Sunday's sessions; CEO Moustafa Elkamash targets a 70% payout.
calls.view: In a market that lost about EGP 142bn of value in a day and leans on margin, a EGP 10bn state sale draws cash from mid-caps until it prices; a well-covered book would show buyers are still there. At about 12 times 2025 profit of EGP 5.8bn it is priced for its dividend, not for growth. Low confidence: the price is not final.
calls.wrong: The EGX70 EWI closes above 18,000 before the offer prices.

calls.headline: Telecom Egypt holds flat as 205 stocks fall, a week before MSCI
calls.line: Unchanged at EGP 137.00 while the EGX30 lost 2.85%; index funds buy it at the November 30 close.
calls.body: Telecom Egypt closed at EGP 137.00, unchanged, and EFG Holding at EGP 25.50, the only desk stocks not to fall on Sunday, while Eastern Company lost 4.3% to EGP 32.60 (Arab Finance, Mubasher). MSCI adds Telecom Egypt to its Egypt standard index and removes Eastern at the November 30 close.
calls.view: Holding flat on a day that took 205 stocks down is what known index demand looks like: funds that must buy on November 30 give the stock a floor the rest of the market lacks. The desk keeps its view that it holds its ground into the inclusion. Medium confidence.
calls.wrong: It closes below EGP 122 before November 30.

calls.headline: SEC probe report sinks Nvidia 14%; S&P 500's worst week since 2020
calls.body: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910.39 on Friday, the Nasdaq 5.28% to 22,617.73 and the Dow 1.93% to 48,147.33; the S&P 500 and the Dow closed in correction, the S&P's seventh straight fall was its longest since February 2020, and the Nasdaq erased its gain for the year (CNN, Reuters via Business Times). Nvidia fell 14% to $125.53, erasing about $491bn of market value, after Reuters reported, citing two people briefed, that the SEC is examining its accounting (Yahoo Finance, Finimize). The VIX closed at 35.89 (Cboe).
calls.view: The report turns a valuation reset into a question about the quality of AI earnings, which is harder to buy on a dip: until Nvidia or the SEC says more, the desk expects the AI leaders to keep lagging steady earners into November 27, its open rotation view. Medium confidence: after seven straight falls and an RSI of 15 on Nvidia, a sharp relief rally can come at any time, so the test is relative.
calls.wrong: The Nasdaq closes above 24,000 before November 27.

calls.headline: Broadcom drops 12% on a report Google trims 2027 TPU orders
calls.line: Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said Google is moving part of its 2027 TPU volume to MediaTek; neither company has confirmed it.
calls.body: Broadcom fell 12.2% to $304.41 after analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said Google is shifting part of its planned 2027 TPU orders to MediaTek (24/7 Wall St, MLQ); TipRanks put the cut at about 20%. Neither company has confirmed it, and Goldman Sachs kept a $460 target. Marvell fell about 10% (24/7 Wall St). Broadcom's AI chip revenue grew 221% in its fiscal third quarter.
calls.view: A survey-based analyst note is not an order book, but it hits the custom-chip case at its weakest moment, with buyers already questioning AI budgets. The desk expects Broadcom to trade with Nvidia rather than recover on its own over the next two weeks. Low confidence: a denial from Google would reverse much of the fall.

calls.headline: Investors buy Treasuries: the 10-year falls to 4.92%, the VIX to 35.89
calls.line: Haven buying pulled the 10-year yield down 12 basis points on Friday, though futures still price a December hike.
calls.body: The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.92% on Friday from 5.04% on Thursday (Treasury), about 20 basis points lower on the week as the AI selloff drove money into government debt (Stocktwits via TradingView), and the VIX closed at 35.89 (Cboe). Futures still put about 95% odds on a quarter-point hike on December 9, after minutes showed nearly all officials expecting one (CME FedWatch, per the newsletter's recap).
calls.view: Lower yields here come from fear, not from a softer Fed: the hike is still priced. The desk expects that to help housing and small caps less than the yield move suggests, until Wednesday's PCE release shows whether the Fed's case holds. Low confidence: a soft PCE print would pull hike odds down quickly.
calls.wrong: Futures cut the odds of a December hike below 50% before December 9.

calls.headline: Global Payments jumps 9.9% on a report GTCR weighs a $50bn buyout
calls.line: Its largest shareholder is weighing a takeover valued at about $50bn including debt; a report, not an offer.
calls.body: Global Payments rose 9.95% to $91.83 after a report that GTCR, its largest shareholder with about 16%, is weighing a full takeover valued at about $50bn including debt (Seeking Alpha via TradingView, Yahoo Finance); the stock had been up about 14% during the session. No offer has been made.
calls.view: A private-equity bid in a week like this shows buyers paying for steady cash flows the market is selling with everything else, which fits the desk's steady-earner case. The desk does not expect a deal to be announced soon. Low confidence: financing a $50bn buyout with the 10-year near 5% is hard.
calls.wrong: Global Payments closes below $84 before December 31.

drivers.name: A stronger dollar abroad

drivers.why: $13bn in July–September, up 20.4%, and $38.2bn in nine months, the economy's largest single source of dollars (central bank via EnterpriseAM).

drivers.name: LNG imports at a higher price
drivers.why: Three LNG cargoes bound for Egypt turned away as Europe paid more (EnterpriseAM, one report), so replacing them costs dollars; Brent at $92.57 is about 22% below its October 30 peak.

view.headline: The IMF vote keeps the dollar in EGP 53–56
view.body: The pound gave up 1.2% in one step to EGP 54.50 as US yields near 5% and an expected Fed hike narrowed the carry, and import and debt payments drew on dollars. The IMF board's vote on the final review, worth up to $2.3bn before December 15, record remittances and the $3bn of planned international issues should keep it within EGP 53–56; the state's willingness to pay 26.29% on bills keeps foreign holders paid to stay.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 56 before December 15, or the IMF board delays the review.

news.headline: Intel signs its first outside customer for 18A chipmaking
news.text: Chief executive Lip-Bu Tan said on November 18 that Intel had signed the first customer for its 18A process; it also widened a supply deal with Microsoft.

global.finding: Gold rebounded about 3% to near $3,630 in futures on Monday after Friday's 4.6% fall to $3,515.40, and Bitcoin recovered to about $61,450 from a Saturday low near $55,000; South Korea's KOSPI still closed 3.3% lower.

notes.brent: Egypt imports fuel and LNG, so Brent at $92.57, down 3.4% on the week on surplus forecasts, eases the import bill; Saturday's Houthi missiles at Riyadh have not yet traded.
notes.gold_usd: Sets the base for Egyptian gold: the 24K gram rose 2.0% to EGP 6,365 on Monday as the ounce rebounded and the pound weakened.
notes.dxy: 103.81 at Friday's close, near its highest since April 2025 as December hike bets held; the pound slipped to EGP 54.50.
notes.btc: A gauge of risk appetite: about $61,450 on Monday, up 4.1%, after a Saturday low near $55,000.

news.headline: KOSPI closes 3.3% lower after a 5.8% plunge on AI fears
news.text: Samsung Electronics fell 3.1% and SK Hynix 2.5%; Hong Kong's Hang Seng slipped 0.1% after falling nearly 2%, while US tech futures pointed higher.

news.headline: Two tankers hit in Hormuz as Qatari mediators visit Tehran
news.text: Two tankers were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday, a maritime monitor said, as Iran announced talks with a Qatari delegation; US-Iran negotiations have stalled.

news.headline: Brent edges up to $92.57 but posts a third weekly loss
news.text: Buying before Thanksgiving and Iran-war worries lifted it 59 cents late on Friday; it fell 3.4% on the week as the IEA sees a surplus.

news.headline: Gold falls to a 14-month low on Fed hike bets
news.text: Gold dropped below $3,650 early on Friday as futures priced a December hike, and settled 4.6% lower at $3,515.40.

news.headline: Saudi Arabia intercepts three Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh
news.text: The second attack on the Saudi capital in three days, after a missile damaged the PIF Tower on November 19; no casualties were reported.

news.headline: Russian missiles come down in Poland; NATO calls it a grave violation
news.text: Poland said two Kh-101 cruise missiles and a drone fell on its territory during an attack on Ukraine; it asked allies for more air defenses.
